A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DistR framework and retain matching theoretical and experimental material. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on image and genomic datasets, including benchmark scores, runtime comparisons, and hyperbolic embeddings in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds kernel comparisons and sensitivity experiments in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The generic DistR objective, alternating embedding/coupling optimization, and mirror-descent and conditional-gradient updates are retained. v3 explicitly instantiates the already general loss/similarity framework for UMAP and tests alternative initialization; these do not introduce a new optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight image/genomic dataset evaluations, toy examples, and Euclidean and hyperbolic embedding tasks. Table 1 retains the dataset sizes and class counts. Added kernels, clustering choices, and embedding dimensions change configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 uses spectral clustering in the DR→C and C→DR comparators; v3 additionally evaluates Kmeans versions of both pipelines in Appendix F.7. COOT and the original comparators remain. Kmeans already appeared as a downstream evaluation algorithm, but its participation in these comparator pipelines is new.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands evaluation configurations with ordinary t-SNE and UMAP kernels, alternative clustering/initialization, and dimensions d = 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 on COIL, SNA1, and PBMC. Equations (81)–(82) revise the written silhouette definition, and Appendix F.9 now states that timing excludes low-rank factorization. These reported protocol changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds spectral-versus-Kmeans ablations for sequential pipelines and DistR initialization (Appendix F.7, Figure 15), plus embedding-dimension sensitivity analysis (F.8, Figure 16). The ordinary t-SNE and UMAP comparisons also examine dependence on the original SEA choice. These substantially broaden checks beyond the retained granularity and hyperbolic analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs or initializations and retain the same percentile-based uncertainty displays and parenthesized table values. Added comparisons also report five-run summaries where specified. No increased run count, new seed disclosure, significance test, or uncertainty estimator is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the matched PCA, SEA, runtime, and hyperbolic plots retain their results. v3 adds extensive ordinary t-SNE and UMAP results in Figures 6, 9, and 10, plus clustering and dimension results in Figures 15–16. For example, Appendix F.7 reports a better average trade-off for spectral-clustering initialization of DistR than Kmeans initialization. These are added findings, not improvements to the original same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The main theorems and their proofs are retained under appendix renumbering. v3 adds a BCE loss decomposition, a spectral-error/eigenvalue identity in Section 4.2, and corrections to the weighted-silhouette definition. The new spectral identity's weight normalization does not match the retained expression in Appendix D.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claim of unifying dimensionality reduction and clustering remain unchanged. The introduction narrows its novelty claim from the DR–OT link having not been explored to being less explored, acknowledging concurrent work while distinguishing DistR's broader scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds graph-coarsening and spectrum-preservation interpretations beyond the earlier kernel-kmeans connection. Appendix F.7 interprets how clustering choices affect the competing pipelines, and Section 5 discusses dimension stability. Existing qualifications about theoretical applicability and hyperbolic curvature remain.

D1.justification: v2 says code accompanies the submission; v3 supplies an explicit repository link in Section 5. v3 also documents UMAP parameter fitting and the BCE decomposition, and expands kernel and timing descriptions. Some added details are inconsistent: Appendix F.10 mentions a Gaussian kernel while retaining H-Student wording, and F.9 excludes low-rank factorization while retaining a speed explanation invoking it.

R1.justification: v3 adds Clark et al. (2024) and Murray and Pickarski (2024), distinguishing their concurrent multidimensional-scaling work from DistR's broader DR/clustering framework. It also adds Loukas (2019) for graph reduction. The remaining research positioning is largely retained.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative and most prose remain. v3 makes local rewrites, expands explanations, adds acknowledgments and experimental subsections, and introduces an appendix overview that shifts the original appendices from A–E to B–F. This is limited restructuring rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds multi-panel Figures 6, 9, 10, 15, and 16, swaps the order of the original Figures 4 and 5, and reduces the main score display from five dataset columns to three while retaining complete appendix results. Journal formatting also resizes and relocates figures and tables and expands captions, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 better supports the framework's generality through ordinary t-SNE/UMAP experiments and clustering/dimension sensitivity checks, while improving code-access information and novelty positioning. These provide a limited overall gain beyond the retained core evidence. The benefit is tempered by conflicting new kernel and timing descriptions and the added spectral identity's normalization inconsistency with Appendix D.
